stories.label: Iran carries out strike on US airbase  --  IRGC
stories.summary: IRGC announces a retaliatory strike on a US airbase in Kuwait after a US strike near Bandar Abbas Airport — the war is now hitting US installations on Arab soil. Lead with who escalated and the target: an OIC Gulf state's territory has been turned into a US-Iran battlefield without Kuwait's consent. Mechanism: tit-for-tat strikes have moved past Iranian and Israeli soil and onto the host countries the US uses to project force, putting Gulf populations directly in the crossfire of a war they did not declare. Continues the Iran-war arc but pivots it onto Kuwait — the next country dragged in after Oman was threatened yesterday.

stories.label: Why a US-Iran deal no longer matters
stories.summary: An Egyptian regional voice argues that after two wars and weeks of leaks, any US-Iran deal Trump now signs is downstream of facts already created on the ground — energy markets reshuffled, Lebanon being bombed, Gaza still besieged. Lead with the regional vantage: this is how the Middle East reads a Washington-Tehran handshake when its own cities have already paid the bill. Mechanism to teach — diplomatic agreements ratify rather than reverse the new map; the leverage shifted before the ink dried. Mada Masr is the Cairo-based investigative outlet most Muslim-world readers trust to interpret Iran-war diplomacy without Beltway framing.

stories.label: A Textbook Debate: Why Russian Historians Told Kyrgyz Historians to Ditch the Term 'Colonialism'
stories.summary: Russian academics formally pressured Kyrgyz counterparts to drop 'colonialism' from school textbooks describing the Tsarist and Soviet conquest of Central Asia. Lead with the move itself: Moscow is policing not the borders of Kyrgyzstan but its history curriculum, because a state that names its past as colonised tomorrow can name its present that way too. Mechanism to teach — soft power is enforced through joint commissions, peer review and 'historian dialogue', and that quiet infrastructure is how an OIC-region republic's narrative independence is contested without a single soldier. Reader: this is the post-Soviet Muslim world's textbook front, often invisible to Western coverage.

stories.label: Mideast war reshaping national energy strategies: IEA
stories.summary: IEA chief calls this 'the largest energy security crisis the world has ever faced' and says countries are opening new supply routes and falling back on domestic resources — including coal — to ride out the Mideast war. Lead with the IEA's own language: the agency built to manage the 1970s oil shock has declared this one larger. Mechanism to teach — energy 'transition' planning is being overwritten in real time by Hormuz-driven supply fear, and the immediate winner is coal, not renewables. Multi-sourced TR/US (Bloomberg)/Middle East Eye, with strong sentiment divergence between Western and regional outlets on how to frame the same crisis.

stories.label: India-US Trade Talks Resume June 1 As Both Sides Push For Interim Deal
stories.summary: India and the US restart trade negotiations in New Delhi on June 1, aiming for an interim deal covering market access, tariffs, investment and security. Lead with what is actually on the table — security is now tied to the trade text, a pattern the US has used to extract supply-chain and tech-export concessions from partners. Mechanism to teach — 'interim' deals lock in concessions that the broader deal then ratifies, so the negotiating ground for the bigger pact is being decided next week. Reader takeaway: India's calculation of how far to bend on tariffs is being made under the shadow of a US that is rewriting partner relationships across Asia.

stories.label: RCEP's moment to matter
stories.summary: The 2027 RCEP General Review is the world's largest trading bloc's only scheduled chance to redesign itself before geoeconomic fragmentation hardens further. Lead with the stake: RCEP covers 15 Asian economies and nearly a third of global GDP, but its rules are thin where they need to be deep (services, digital, state-owned enterprises). Mechanism to teach — the General Review is the moment where members either upgrade the bloc into an anchor against US-China decoupling or let it remain a tariff schedule on autopilot, and the decision is being shaped now, not in 2027. Reader takeaway: while Washington and Beijing fight in the headlines, the next layer of global trade rules is being drafted in committee rooms.

stories.label: Temperatures likely to remain at record levels in 2026-2030: UN
stories.summary: WMO forecasts the next five years will continue at or near record global temperatures — the 11 hottest years on record all fall since 2015, and the trend is now self-sustaining. Lead with the chronological fact: the climate has settled into a new operating range, and the chance of any year before 2030 being 'cooler than recent normal' is essentially zero. Mechanism to teach — once ocean heat content crosses a threshold, year-to-year variability oscillates around a higher mean; what was an extreme decade ago is now baseline. Reader takeaway: every infrastructure, agricultural and public-health plan built around 20th-century temperatures is already obsolete. Carried by Dawn (PK) and Tempo (ID) — Muslim-world heat-vulnerable countries reading the same WMO bulletin.

stories.label: Kenya: Fire kills several at a girls' boarding school
stories.summary: At least 16 students killed and 73 injured in a pre-dawn fire at a girls' boarding school in Gilgil, central Kenya. Lead with the named place and the children: this is the second major Kenyan boarding-school fire in three years, and the country's safety regulations after the 2023 Hillside Endarasha disaster were supposed to prevent exactly this. Mechanism to teach — Kenyan dormitories are typically locked at night for discipline; in a fire, that turns rooms into death traps. Accountability frame: the regulator and ministry of education are both named in past inquests and have repeatedly missed compliance deadlines. The victims are African schoolgirls who deserve the same naming and grieving Western readers give to Western tragedies.

stories.label: Q&A: Can China turn hydrogen into its next clean-energy industry?
stories.summary: Beijing has named hydrogen a key 'future industry' alongside solar, batteries and EVs — the categories where China already dominates global supply. Lead with the pattern: every time China labels a sector strategic, the rest of the world later finds itself buying that technology from Chinese suppliers, and hydrogen electrolysers are the next test. Mechanism to teach — the policy stack is industrial subsidy + grid integration + scale demand from steel and chemicals, the same recipe that crushed Western solar manufacturers. Reader takeaway: 'clean hydrogen' will arrive faster than Western forecasts expect, and the supplier of the electrolysers is being decided right now.

stories.label: Wearables and women's healthtech: advancing measurement, monitoring and action via digital medicine
stories.summary: A Nature Reviews paper documents that the $50bn-and-growing women's healthtech market — wearables, sensors, cycle and pregnancy trackers — is running on algorithms trained on men's physiology. Lead with the gap, because it is the news: the bias is not editorial but in the training data and validation cohorts, so devices marketed to women are systematically less accurate for them. Mechanism to teach — medical-device regulation does not require sex-stratified validation for consumer wearables, so the gap compounds with every new product cycle. Reader takeaway: the 'quantified self' for half the population is being built on numbers that don't fit them.

stories.label: Romanian national sentenced to more than 4 years for hacking Oregon government systems
stories.summary: A Romanian national, arrested in Romania in November 2024 and extradited, was sentenced to over four years for hacking Oregon's Office of Emergency Management. Lead with the chain: the US is now routinely extraditing Eastern European hackers and getting prison terms, a pattern that did not exist five years ago. Mechanism to teach — bilateral mutual-legal-assistance treaties and EU cooperation have closed the safe-haven gap that defined ransomware-era cybercrime, but Russia-aligned jurisdictions remain immune. Reader takeaway: the geography of who can be prosecuted now maps directly onto the geography of who is aligned with Washington.

stories.label: Palestinians mourn slain Hamas militant chief as Israel escalates Gaza attacks
stories.summary: Israel killed Mohammad Odeh in a targeted strike — the second Hamas military chief eliminated in a week after Izz al-Din al-Haddad. Lead with the mechanism: serial decapitation strikes paired with escalating ground attacks, leaving few senior commanders to negotiate any ceasefire. Frame around the named victims and the strategic cost of removing every interlocutor while siege continues.

stories.label: No feasts, no joy: Gazans mark a dark Eid
stories.summary: Eid al-Adha in Gaza: no sheep, no new clothes, no biscuits — markets exist only as windows to look at unaffordable goods. Lead with the symbolic weight of a Muslim festival of sacrifice rendered impossible by siege. The dignity frame: this is not deprivation as side-effect but as policy outcome. Regional outlet (Dawn) carrying the story matters for OIC-reader credibility.

stories.label: Google engineer insider-traded search results on Polymarket, Feds allege
stories.summary: A Google security engineer allegedly bet on Polymarket using internal search-trend data — the second major insider-trading arrest in prediction markets. Lead with the mechanism: when speculative markets price 'what people are searching,' the platform's own employees become the ultimate insiders. Accountability angle: prediction markets as a new attack surface that securities law is only just catching up to.

stories.label: California to impose 100% tax on Trump's January 6 'slush fund,' governor says
stories.summary: Newsom proposes a 100% state tax on any California resident receiving payouts from Trump's planned January 6 compensation fund — using tax law as counter-attack against a federal policy California considers a 'slush fund' for insurrectionists. Lead with the mechanism: state taxation as constitutional pushback against federal pardons-with-cash. Precedent-setting on federalism.

stories.label: Can Syria's Trains Get Back on Track?
stories.summary: Gulf-to-Mediterranean overland corridor plans cast Syria as a logistics hub — but the railways are bombed-out and the rolling stock is decades old. Lead with the gap between geopolitical ambition (Gulf capital, Chinese-style infrastructure dreams) and ground reality (no working signals, no spare parts, no trained crews). Mechanism: who finances reconstruction and on what terms determines who controls the future trade route through Syria.

stories.label: The Iran War Is Crushing Nebraska Workers. Dan Osborn Is One of Them
stories.summary: Fertilizer and energy input prices surging because of the Iran war are wiping out Nebraska farmers operating on razor margins. Lead with the supply chain: U.S. agriculture depends on natural gas for nitrogen fertilizer, and the Hormuz disruption has reset global prices. Mechanism story: a war 11,000 km away bankrupting Midwest farms — the same systemic-dependency lens as the earlier SadaPay/AWS Bahrain story.

stories.label: Australia to sue 3M for $2bn over 'forever chemicals' in firefighting foam
stories.summary: Australia's largest-ever damages claim — AU$2 billion against 3M for PFAS contamination of dozens of defence bases. Lead with the science: 'forever chemicals' don't degrade, the firefighting foam was used for decades, and the contamination is now in groundwater and bloodstreams of base-adjacent communities. Accountability angle: a state suing a foreign manufacturer for known toxicity sets a template other governments will copy.

stories.label: Deep learning-based forecasting provides a pathway to closing wildfire information gaps in underserved regions
stories.summary: A new deep-learning wildfire forecast model trained on ECMWF data can predict fire spread in regions without weather stations or fire agencies — most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. Lead with the asymmetry: rich countries have radar networks, poor countries have satellite-trained models inferring from physics. Mechanism: closes the prediction gap that has left underserved regions reactive rather than prepared for climate-amplified fire.

stories.label: Internet partially restored in Iran after months-long shutdown
stories.summary: Iran restored partial international connectivity after a near-three-month total shutdown imposed when the US-Israel war began on Feb 28. Lead with the duration: 90 days of intranet-only — banking, messaging, work all forced onto domestic platforms — which becomes the new permanent infrastructure even after restoration. Mechanism: wartime shutdowns serve as forced migration to surveillance-friendly national stacks. Regional voice (Dawn) covering the story for Muslim-world readers.

stories.label: Pope Leo XIV: AI Wealth Must Be Universally Shared
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV publicly argues AI's productivity gains belong to humanity, not the labs that own the compute. Lead with the moral framing from a religious authority entering an industrial-policy debate dominated by venture capitalists. Mechanism: Vatican social teaching applied to compute — places the labor-vs-capital question at the center of AI distribution, a frame echoed in Islamic economic thought on zakat and wealth circulation.

stories.label: AI is not the answer to AI-enabled fraud
stories.summary: Standard Chartered's CEO called compliance staff 'lower-value human capital' as he plans to replace them with AI — exposing that banks already treated their fraud-prevention humans like inefficient computers. Lead with the quote, then the mechanism: AI fraud is exploding precisely because human judgment has been stripped out of compliance for a decade; doubling down on automation accelerates the failure. Accountability frame: when the chief of fraud-prevention dehumanizes his own department, regulators should pay attention.

stories.label: After Iran showdown, Trump threatens to blow up Oman for this reason
stories.summary: Trump threatened military force against Oman if it partners with Iran to oversee Strait of Hormuz traffic. The surprise is the target: Oman is the Gulf's neutral mediator — the channel through which the US-Iran ceasefire talks themselves run — and Washington is now treating the broker as an enemy. Lead with a US president threatening to bomb an OIC state that has fired no shot; mechanism to teach is how control of Hormuz is being converted into a pretext to discipline any state that won't take sides. Continues the Iran-war arc but pivots it onto a new country — keep it as the single Iran-adjacent slot this cycle.

stories.label: Trump's Board of Peace is flailing - just like the president
stories.summary: The World Bank fund for Trump's Gaza 'Board of Peace' has received exactly zero dollars despite $17 billion in pledges from the US and others, an FT scoop confirms. Lead with the gap between the pledge total and the empty account: reconstruction announcements without escrow are a form of theatre, and Gazans living in rubble are the ones metering the difference. Mechanism to teach — pledged aid is a headline; deposited aid is a transfer, and the distance between them is where political credit is claimed without cost. Who is affected: Palestinians waiting on a fund that exists only on paper. Sourced IL/GB/IN/SG — note the feed carried no Arab regional outlet on this Gaza-fund cluster.

stories.label: Ghanaians flee SA as fear of xenophobic violence grows
stories.summary: A plane carrying 300 Ghanaians — women and children among them — landed in Accra, evacuated from South Africa as anti-immigrant protests escalate. Lead with the repatriation flight itself: when a government charters planes to pull its citizens out of another African state, the 'protest' has crossed into a threat to life. Mechanism to teach — South Africa's economic strain is being displaced onto migrant Africans, and the continent's most industrialised state is now exporting its own citizens' fear back to poorer neighbours. Who is affected: West African migrants and the Pan-African promise that the AU's open-borders rhetoric was supposed to protect. Carried QA/ZA; feed offered no Ghanaian outlet.

stories.label: Police enter Spain's ruling party HQ in graft probe
stories.summary: Spain's Civil Guard entered the headquarters of Sánchez's governing Socialist party on Calle de Ferraz, executing an Audiencia Nacional judge's order in the funding probe centred on former party number-three Santos Cerdán. Lead with the image of uniformed police inside a sitting government's party HQ: the corruption investigation has reached the building, not just the man. Mechanism to teach — Spain's investigating-magistrate system lets a judge order searches of the ruling party while it governs, a separation-of-powers stress test most parliamentary systems never run. Who holds power and who checks it: the PM keeps backing an ex-leader the courts are pursuing. Multi-sourced IT/GB/IN/TR/MY.

stories.label: Nvidia bets $150B on Taiwan as Trump's plan to make US an AI hub backfires
stories.summary: Jensen Huang said Nvidia will spend $150 billion a year to keep Taiwan the 'epicenter' of the AI revolution — a direct rebuff to Trump's effort to relocate the AI supply chain to American soil. Lead with the number and who said it: the world's most valuable chip designer is voting with its capital for Taiwan over Washington's industrial policy. Mechanism to teach — chip geography is set by TSMC's irreplaceable fabrication ecosystem, not by tariffs or subsidies, so the US can fund domestic plants and still find the centre of gravity stays in Taipei. Reader takeaway: 'AI sovereignty' rhetoric runs into the hard physics of where chips can actually be made, and that pins the Pacific's most dangerous flashpoint to the global economy.

stories.label: World Cup 2026: Fifa summoned to explain ticket pricing
stories.summary: New York's attorney general subpoenaed FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing after a charity for spinal-injury patients was forced to cancel a ticket raffle by cease-and-desist letters. Lead with the contrast: FIFA's lawyers shut down a disabled-persons' fundraiser while a state AG demands FIFA explain its own dynamic-pricing scheme. Mechanism to teach — FIFA holds a monopoly on the scarcest tickets in sport and runs algorithmic surge pricing, and the legal pressure point is consumer-protection and antitrust law, not football governance. Who holds power: a supranational body answerable to no national regulator, now being tested by one. Multi-sourced US/GB/TR.

stories.label: Brazil to invest $75 million in highway through Amazon and unveils environmental protection plan
stories.summary: Lula's government will spend $75 million paving the BR-319 through the Amazon, branding it the 'most environmentally advanced road in the world' even as scientists warn paved roads are the single strongest predictor of deforestation. Lead with the contradiction at the heart of the announcement: a climate-forward president underwriting the one piece of infrastructure that reliably opens rainforest to clearing. Mechanism to teach — roads don't cut trees, but they collapse the cost of reaching untouched forest, so the 'protection plan' is fighting an incentive the asphalt itself creates. Who is affected: the Amazon biome and the global carbon budget that Brazil's own diplomacy claims to defend. Mongabay is the field's source of record here.

stories.label: Websites have a new way to spy on visitors: analyzing their SSD activity
stories.summary: Researchers showed websites can fingerprint and track visitors by measuring timing patterns in their device's SSD activity — a hardware side channel no privacy setting blocks. Lead with the dead end it creates for the reader: clearing cookies, blocking scripts and using a VPN do nothing against a method that reads the physical behaviour of your storage. Mechanism to teach — side-channel attacks infer secrets from how fast operations run, and as browsers closed older fingerprinting vectors, trackers moved down the stack to the hardware itself. Who holds power: the same ad-tech and platform players (Meta, Yandex already caught) racing browser defenders one layer at a time. The reader is a developer who needs to know the surveillance arms race has reached the SSD.

stories.label: 'Lobotomized': Character.AI Is Showing What AI Enshittification Looks Like
stories.summary: Character.AI users are revolting after ads, usage caps, tighter guardrails and reduced model choice made the app they relied on visibly worse. Lead with the pattern, because it is the news: this is the first major consumer-AI product to run the full 'enshittification' cycle — court users, then degrade the product to extract revenue. Mechanism to teach — venture-subsidised AI tools were priced below cost to build dependence, and the bill is now arriving as the same degradation that hit social platforms, only faster because inference is expensive. Who is affected: millions of users, many of them emotionally attached to chatbot companions, learning that the product is a rented experience the company can quietly downgrade. 404 Media owns this beat.

stories.label: DeFi isn't safe anymore because AI is becoming 'superhuman' at hacking, onetime OpenZeppelin founder says
stories.summary: A founder of OpenZeppelin — the firm that audits much of DeFi's code — warns that AI models can now autonomously discover and weaponise software flaws faster than humans can patch them, leaving transparent on-chain code newly indefensible. Lead with the asymmetry: DeFi's design virtue, fully public smart contracts, becomes a liability the moment an attacker's AI can read every line and find the bug first. Mechanism to teach — automated exploit discovery collapses the window between disclosure and attack, and DeFi has no patch-and-restart; funds drain in one transaction. Who is affected: anyone holding assets in smart contracts, and the broader software world that is about to face the same attacker speed. Reader takeaway: AI-vs-AI security is arriving first where the code and the money are both public.

stories.label: Heart patch engineered from stem cells revved up weakened hearts
stories.summary: A heart patch grown from stem cells strengthened the pumping of damaged hearts in a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine — a step toward repairing muscle the heart cannot regenerate on its own. Lead with the long-standing wall this breaks: after a heart attack the heart heals with scar, not muscle, and nothing in standard care reverses that loss. Mechanism to teach — lab-grown cardiomyocytes are sewn onto the failing wall as a living graft that contributes contractile force, turning regeneration from a metaphor into engineered tissue. Who is affected: heart failure is the world's leading killer, and this is the rare cardiovascular advance that adds muscle rather than merely slowing decline. Reader takeaway: the evidence has reached a top-tier journal, the threshold where a therapy stops being a press release.

stories.label: Researchers push back fundamental limit on energy transfer between particles without 'spilling' radiation
stories.summary: A TU Eindhoven team moved energy between particles over several millimetres with almost no loss to stray light or heat — using vibrations in microscopic gold rods — far beyond the distance physicists thought possible. Lead with the textbook limit it overturns: near-field energy transfer was assumed to die off within nanometres, and this stretches it by orders of magnitude. Mechanism to teach — coupling the particles through mechanical vibration channels the energy along a path that doesn't 'spill' into radiation, the leakage that normally caps efficiency. Who benefits: anyone designing energy harvesting, photonics, or chip-scale heat management, where loss over distance is the binding constraint. Reader takeaway: a quiet result that redraws one of the boundary conditions engineers design against.

stories.label: Risk factors associated with rectal carriage of extended spectrum beta-lactamases producing Enterobacterales among inpatients at a tertiary hospital in Northern Nigeria: A cross-sectional study - Scientific Reports
stories.summary: A cross-sectional study at a Northern Nigeria tertiary hospital measured how many inpatients silently carry ESBL-producing Enterobacterales — gut bacteria armed with enzymes that defeat front-line antibiotics — and which patients are most at risk. Lead with the hidden reservoir: drug-resistant bugs colonise patients before they ever cause an infection, and that carriage is the engine of hospital outbreaks. Mechanism to teach — antimicrobial resistance is concentrated in low- and middle-income countries where antibiotic access outpaces lab surveillance, so the carriers go uncounted until a resistant infection turns untreatable. Who is affected: patients in the very hospitals meant to heal them, and a global resistance problem whose frontline data comes from places rarely funded to collect it. Reader takeaway: the next pandemic-grade threat is being measured one ward at a time in Kano.

stories.label: The 'Lost' Villages of Myanmar's Rakhine
stories.summary: Bellingcat geolocates and verifies villages erased in western Myanmar — a survivor describes a 'river of blood', and 20 relatives including three children killed in a 2024 attack on Htan Shauk Khan. Lead with the named village and the satellite-before/after method: this is OSINT making the disappearance of Rohingya-area settlements legally legible when no court will name it. Mechanism to highlight: physical erasure of villages is the form ethnic cleansing takes once the cameras leave, and Bellingcat's frames are the documentary record that survives. The reader cares because the victims are Muslims the world stopped counting.

stories.label: US strike on alleged drug boat in Pacific kills one
stories.summary: A US military strike on a vessel it labelled a 'narco-terrorist' boat in the Eastern Pacific killed one man and left two stranded at sea — the latest in a pattern rights groups are tracking. Lead with the legal void: there was no arrest, no court, no due process, just a lethal strike on a suspected smuggler, and the Pentagon's own language ('narco-terrorist') is the tell that a law-enforcement problem has been redefined as a war target. Mechanism to teach: the post-9/11 'targeted killing' doctrine built for jihadists is migrating to drug interdiction in international waters, normalising extrajudicial execution of civilians. Al Jazeera carries it because Western wires treat the body count as routine.

stories.label: Hungary Reverses Decision to Exit International Criminal Court
stories.summary: Hungary's parliament repealed the ICC-withdrawal Orbán launched in 2025 as a gesture to Netanyahu — and the reversal comes under new PM Péter Magyar. Lead with what changed and what it signals: a single election unwound a member state's exit from the world's only permanent war-crimes court, and Israeli press is reading it as the loss of a friendly carve-out for an indicted PM. Mechanism to teach: the ICC's authority is only as durable as the domestic politics of its members, and the same machinery that nearly let Hungary shield Netanyahu can be switched off by the next government. Multi-sourced across HU, US, IL, SG and ZA — note the symmetry of how each capital frames a court that indicts the powerful.

stories.label: Big setback for opposition as Supreme Court upholds Election Commission's power to conduct S.I.R exercise
stories.summary: India's Supreme Court ruled the Election Commission acted within its powers in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, dismissing opposition petitions that the Bihar exercise risked disenfranchising voters by tying the rolls to citizenship checks. Lead with the precedent, not the politics: a court with the power to halt a roll purge instead blessed it, and that ruling now governs how every future revision can be run ahead of national elections. Mechanism to teach: who controls the voter list controls the electorate, and the SIR converts an administrative cleanup into a citizenship gate the judiciary has now declared constitutional. The reader should see this as a structural shift in Indian electoral plumbing, carried across three Indian outlets with low divergence.

stories.label: Typical energy bill set to soar by £221 a year from July as new price cap announced
stories.summary: Ofgem's new price cap lifts the typical UK household bill by £221 a year from July — the first time the Iran war's wholesale-gas spike lands directly on domestic bills. Lead with the transmission chain: a war 4,000km away over the Strait of Hormuz now shows up as a line item on a British variable tariff, and the Guardian's analyst says high prices are structural, not a spike. Mechanism to teach: the UK's exposure to global gas means its consumers are unhedged buyers of Middle East risk, and 'energy security' rhetoric has not insulated a single household. The reader sees how a geopolitical shock is metered out to ordinary people through a regulator's quarterly arithmetic.

stories.label: Byju's founder Byju Raveendran gets six-month jail term in Singapore
stories.summary: A Singapore court jailed Byju Raveendran for six months for contempt — defying asset-related court orders dating to 2024 — closing a chapter on what was once India's most-valuable startup, backed by the Qatar Investment Authority among others. Lead with the fall: a founder once worth billions on paper is going to jail not for the collapse itself but for stonewalling the courts unwinding it. Mechanism to teach: when a venture-capital darling implodes, the accountability that bites is cross-border insolvency enforcement, and Singapore's contempt power reached a founder Indian proceedings could not. The reader sees the edtech bubble's reckoning arrive through a jurisdiction chosen for its rigour, not its sympathy.

stories.label: Hong Kong beats Switzerland as world's largest offshore wealth hub, BCG finds
stories.summary: BCG data shows Hong Kong has overtaken Switzerland as the world's largest cross-border wealth hub, with offshore money booked there up 10.7% in 2025 to US$2.9 trillion on mainland inflows and an IPO bonanza. Lead with the handover of a centuries-old title: the global capital of hidden money is no longer the Alps but a Chinese SAR. Mechanism to teach: offshore wealth follows political gravity — capital is choosing a jurisdiction inside China's perimeter over neutral Switzerland, a vote about where the rich think safety and growth now sit. The reader sees the financial centre of the next era being named in a consulting firm's league table.

stories.label: Synthetic controls reveal hurricane effects on urban bee biodiversity from iNaturalist data - Nature Ecology & Evolution
stories.summary: Researchers paired citizen-science iNaturalist observations with synthetic-control methods — an econometrics tool — to show Hurricane Ida cut bee observations in Philadelphia by 15.5–20.9%. Lead with the method, because that is the news: causal inference borrowed from economics now lets ecologists measure a single disaster's hit to urban biodiversity from messy public data. Mechanism to teach: synthetic controls build a 'counterfactual city' from comparison sites, isolating the storm's effect from background noise — the same technique that evaluates policy, applied to pollinators. The reader gets why this matters: it turns the flood of amateur nature photos into rigorous evidence of how climate shocks erode the species cities depend on.

stories.label: U.S. companies have an AI problem. Indian IT wants to be the solution
stories.summary: As US firms find AI returns elusive, India's IT giants are pitching themselves as the integrators who can close the 'deployment gap' — even as the same automation threatens to eat their own back-office business. Lead with the bind: the labour pool that built the West's software is now selling the shovels for an AI gold rush that may bury it. Mechanism to teach: most enterprise AI value is stuck at the last mile of integration, and that messy middle is exactly the outsourcing work India dominates — a reprieve, but one with an expiry date as agents improve. The reader, a technically literate professional, recognises both the ROI mirage and the global-South labour story underneath it.

stories.label: US law enforcement warns of "anti-tech extremism" as AI hatred grows
stories.summary: After attacks on CEOs and a protest movement targeting data centers, US federal intelligence and domestic law enforcement are circulating reports naming a new domestic target: 'anti-technology extremists.' Lead with the move itself — the state is constructing a threat category around opposition to AI and data centers, more than 1,000 documents deep. Mechanism to teach: labelling diffuse public anger as 'extremism' is how surveillance and counterterrorism powers get extended to a political grievance, folding legitimate protest over jobs and land into the security apparatus. The reader should see the civil-liberties stakes: the backlash against AI is being criminalised before it is understood.

stories.label: Tuvalu aims to become a 'Digital Nation' amid rising sea levels
stories.summary: Tuvalu is digitising its statehood — government, records, identity and culture — to preserve sovereignty as rising seas threaten to make the islands uninhabitable. Lead with the unprecedented question it forces: can a nation exist as data when its land disappears? Mechanism to teach: statehood in international law rests on territory and population, so Tuvalu is engineering a legal-technical workaround — a 'Digital Nation' that keeps its maritime boundaries, governance and identity alive in the cloud even if the physical state drowns. The reader sees the first real test of post-territorial sovereignty, a Global-South innovation born of an emergency the world's emitters created.

stories.label: Imaging quantum chemistry in action with quantum attomicroscopy - Communications Chemistry
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for science floor] Understanding how quantum electron and nuclei motions drive biomolecular reactions is a foundational challenge in quantum chemistry and biology. While ultrafast charge migration in DNA is theorized to influence genome stability and signaling, real-time observation remains elusive. Here, we report a

stories.label: SK Hynix Joins $1 Trillion Club on AI Memory Chip Dominance
stories.summary: SK Hynix crossed $1T market cap on HBM dominance and is filing for US ADRs — Korea now hosts the second pure AI-memory monopoly after TSMC. Lead with the structural point: the AI build-out has produced two single-country chokepoints (TSMC logic in Taiwan, SK Hynix HBM in Korea) whose valuations now dwarf entire national markets — pairs with [[taiwan-stock-market-surpasses-india-tsmc-ai-concentration]] as the same concentration story from the demand side. Mechanism: HBM yields favor incumbents because each generation requires deeper integration with NVIDIA's roadmap; Micron and Samsung can't close the gap fast enough to break the duopoly. Reader takeaway: 'AI sovereignty' debates are downstream of two Asian memory and logic fabs.

stories.label: The lender that governs
stories.summary: IMF approved Pakistan's third EFF review and added 11 new conditions — total structural conditionality now 75, with 30 standing commitments for 105 compliance requirements covering fiscal, governance, energy and trade policy. Lead with the number 105: this is no longer a 'loan with conditions', it is a parallel administration that has substituted for elected economic policy-making. Mechanism worth teaching: each review ratchets conditionality upward because compliance gaps from prior reviews are converted into new structural benchmarks — the program grows even when targets are met. Reader takeaway: Pakistan's sovereign budget process now runs through Washington, and Dawn says it plainly. Pakistan OIC; regional voice carried.

stories.label: More Than Trade: Modi's Visit to Sweden and Norway
stories.summary: Modi's Nordic tour is the opening move in India's Arctic strategy — but Russia's existing Arctic dominance is the obstacle Delhi has to negotiate around without breaking its Moscow rapport. Lead with the contradiction: India wants Arctic credentials (rare earths, shipping lanes, scientific stations) but the only northern path runs through Russian-controlled passages. Mechanism worth teaching: the Arctic is becoming the next critical-minerals theatre after Central Asia, and middle powers like India have to choose between US-aligned northern routes and Russian-aligned ones. Pairs with [[india-us-critical-minerals-rare-earths-framework-jaishankar-rubio]] as the parallel polar leg of the same minerals strategy.

stories.label: SPECIAL REPORT: Day Akwa Ibom market burned because a fire truck had no fuel
stories.summary: Premium Times investigation: an Akwa Ibom market burned to the ground because the local fire station had received 'no diesel for over two months' — traders lost stock worth millions of naira while a fueled truck sat idle. Lead with the named station and the two-month gap: this is the accountability failure rendered as a single missing fuel allocation, and Premium Times got the on-the-record admission. Mechanism worth teaching: Nigeria's fiscal devolution after subsidy removal left state-level emergency services unfunded, and the failures are now individually documented — palm oil flowing through burnt walkways while bureaucratic responsibility is dispersed across federal, state and municipal lines no one is willing to claim. Reader takeaway: 'state capacity' is not abstract; it is whether the truck has fuel on the day the market burns. Nigeria OIC; regional voice carried.

stories.label: Bangladesh measles cases: Hundreds of children die within months
stories.summary: Hundreds of Bangladeshi children dead from measles within months — a disease eliminable with a $1 dose. BBC opens on a named 4-year-old, Akira, learning English before she died. Lead with the named child and the count: this is the most preventable mass child death of the season, and it is happening in a country whose vaccination programme was a global model a decade ago. Mechanism worth teaching: measles is a herd-immunity disease, and Bangladesh's coverage dipped below the 95% threshold after pandemic-era catch-up campaigns lapsed and UNICEF funding tightened — the deaths are a delayed externality of a budgeting decision. Reader takeaway: when global vaccine financing slips, the body count appears in the Muslim-majority countries that had been the success cases. Bangladesh OIC.

stories.label: Traveller from Uganda isolated in Bengaluru after showing suspected Ebola symptoms
stories.summary: A woman who flew from Uganda via Ahmedabad to Bengaluru on 23 May was moved to Karnataka's State Epidemic Diseases Hospital after surveillance flagged fatigue and mild symptoms; samples sent to the National Institute of Virology. Lead with the routing — Uganda → Ahmedabad → Bengaluru — and the surveillance trigger: India's Ebola tracking on inbound passengers from affected regions actually caught a suspected case at the airport stage. Mechanism worth teaching: post-2014 international airport surveillance is the single most successful public-health upgrade of the last decade, and most of the catches never make headlines because samples come back negative. Reader takeaway: the system worked here — a suspected case isolated within four days of arrival — and that is the unsexy public-health infrastructure that prevents a second 2014. Flag for follow-up once NIV result is in.

stories.label: Bread&Net 2025: Explore the Outcomes Reports
stories.summary: SMEX publishes the outcome reports from Bread&Net 2025, the MENA region's main digital-rights convening — sessions on infrastructure control, platform takedowns of Arabic and Palestinian content, and surveillance baselines across Lebanon, Egypt, Jordan and the Gulf. Lead with the question the reports keep asking: who controls the digital infrastructure that Arab civil society depends on, and what does the cost of that dependence look like in 2025-2026's documented case data. Mechanism worth teaching: digital-rights work in the MENA region is increasingly a documentation exercise — these outcome reports are the institutional memory that survives even when individual orgs are shut down. Pairs with [[smex-ceasefire-digital-rights-mideast-surveillance-baseline]]. Lebanon OIC; SMEX is the regional voice.

stories.label: Cost To Link LUCAS Kamikaze Drones To Starlink Highlights Pentagon's Ever-Growing Dependence On SpaceX
stories.summary: Pentagon pushes back on reported upcharges to connect LUCAS one-way attack drones to Starlink — but the underlying story is that SpaceX's products have become 'largely essential' to US military operations, with no second supplier at parity. Lead with the lock-in: a single private satellite operator now sets the per-drone connectivity bill for a US weapon system, and the only public negotiation is over the size of the markup. Mechanism worth teaching: defence procurement was supposed to avoid monopoly suppliers by design (DoD Section 803), but LEO broadband is a winner-take-most market and Starlink's lead has converted into a procurement chokepoint the Pentagon admits is irreplaceable. Reader takeaway: 'critical infrastructure' is a category that now includes a private constellation whose owner the US government cannot replace and cannot fully discipline.

stories.label: Iran says new US strikes violate ceasefire
stories.summary: Hours after the Doha track resumed, US CENTCOM ran what it called 'defensive' strikes in southern Iran; Tehran says the truce is already broken and BBC/News18/CNA/Punch carry the same framing with sentimentDivergence 0.24. Lead with the timing collision: Rubio says a deal is 'a few days' away while the kinetic side is still firing, which is precisely the failure mode SMEX and Drop Site have been documenting — a 'ceasefire' that only stops the parts both sides agree to count. Mechanism: 'defensive strikes' is the doctrinal loophole that lets Washington keep shooting and still call it peace, and the political cost is paid by Lebanese and Iranian civilians outside the deal's perimeter. Iran arc continuation from [[iran-mq9-drone-downed-persian-gulf-irgc-ceasefire]] and [[khamenei-no-going-back-us-bases-middle-east-realignment]] — third Iran-arc slot, do not stack further this cycle.

stories.label: US and Armenia sign partnership agreement ahead of Armenian election
stories.summary: Rubio and Mirzoyan signed a strategic-partnership agreement weeks before Armenia votes — multi-sourced from AM, US, SG, IN and TR (Anadolu). Lead with the timing: Washington is putting its name on Pashinyan's re-election platform after Yerevan's pivot away from the CSTO, and Turkey's state wire is reporting it without alarm — which is itself the story, given Ankara and Yerevan's century of frozen diplomacy. Mechanism: 'strategic partnership' is the same template Washington just used with India on rare earths; the Caucasus version trades a sanctions-circumvention chokepoint between Iran and Russia for US security backing. Reader takeaway: the post-Karabakh realignment is being locked in with a US signature, and Iran is reading every line of it.

stories.label: Czech 'ammo coalition' for Ukraine loses support
stories.summary: President Petr Pavel says half the participants — 18 down to 9 countries — have walked away from Prague's Ukraine-ammunition initiative since Babis took office in December 2025, and even RT carries the story straight. Lead with the number: a coalition that was the EU's flagship workaround when Hungary blocked direct aid has been gutted in six months by a single change of government. Mechanism worth teaching: 'coalitions of the willing' depend on whichever election cycle is most recent, and that's a structural weakness Brussels has no answer to. Reader takeaway: the same week US planners briefed NATO they would cut crisis commitments to Europe, Europe's own ad-hoc Ukraine logistics is collapsing — and Moscow is the audience that benefits from both stories landing on the same day.

stories.label: Banned Russian Submunitions Found After Mali's Military Announces Airstrikes
stories.summary: Bellingcat + Jeune Afrique OSINT investigation: unexploded Russian-made cluster bomblets and impact damage documented in a northern Mali village, despite Mali being a state party to the Convention on Cluster Munitions. Lead with the treaty violation by name and the named village: this is the second documented use of banned submunitions by the Bamako–Africa Corps partnership, and the first where the geolocated craters appear in Bellingcat's frames. Mechanism worth teaching: Russia exports the weapons class Western states agreed to stop using, and a Sahelian junta is choosing them precisely because the political cost is paid by villagers no UN body will name. Mali is OIC; feed offered no Malian or regional Sahel outlet — note feed-side gap. Accountability arc, separate from Sudan-RSF-UAE [[sudan-rsf-uae-colombian-mercenaries-hrw-report]] but same supply-chain-of-violence template.

stories.label: Peace deal hopes boost Wall Street stocks despite latest US strikes
stories.summary: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at fresh records the same day US CENTCOM hit Iran and Brent jumped on Hormuz fears — the market is pricing the strikes as a near-term deal catalyst, not an escalation. Lead with the disconnect: equity desks are betting that the next round of strikes shortens the ceasefire negotiation, while oil desks are betting it lengthens it, and both bets are running simultaneously in the same Bloomberg terminal. Mechanism worth teaching: 'risk-on' is now an Iran-war trade, with the Strait of Hormuz functioning as a put option on the broader index — the implied volatility is paid by Global South economies that don't get to hedge. Reader takeaway: the markets that determine US pension performance are now openly priced against the ceasefire holding for the shortest commercially convenient interval.

stories.label: Fatalities Reported in Washington State Packaging Facility Explosion
stories.summary: Nippon Dynawave Packaging's Longview, Washington pulp-and-packaging mill exploded Tuesday morning with fatalities and multiple critical injuries — the second mass-casualty US industrial accident in a working-age industry in six months. Lead with what the facility actually is: pulp mill chemistry runs on hydrogen sulfide, chlorine dioxide and recovery boilers operating just below their explosive limit, and the regulatory deference to operators on the West Coast packaging side is documented. Mechanism worth teaching: 'packaging' sounds benign but the upstream pulping is one of the most dangerous chemical environments outside refining, and federal inspection backlogs at OSHA are running at multi-year highs. Reader takeaway: the workplace-safety regression isn't only a Sahel-mercenary or Kazakh-oil story — it lands the same day in Longview.

stories.label: Govt plans Wapda security force for water projects
stories.summary: Pakistan is creating a dedicated paramilitary 'Wapda Security Force' to protect dams, hydropower plants, and Chinese workers at Dasu and other CPEC-linked sites, following repeated attacks on Chinese engineers. Lead with the institutional choice: water infrastructure has been promoted out of civilian policing and into a standing armed force, with the bill already sent to parliament. Mechanism worth teaching: when a state can no longer guarantee Chinese contractor safety through ordinary means, the contract terms shift — Beijing is increasingly underwriting Pakistani fiscal stress in exchange for sovereign militarisation of CPEC perimeters. Reader takeaway: the cost of CPEC is no longer just the loan book; it is the bureaucratic architecture of a parallel armed force whose mandate is set in Beijing's risk department. Pakistan is OIC; Dawn provides the regional voice.

stories.label: Want an oxygen-rich atmosphere? Stuff oxygen's friends in the mantle.
stories.summary: A new model argues Earth's oxygen-rich atmosphere required not just photosynthesis but a tectonically active mantle willing to swallow reductant minerals — taking oxygen-hungry rocks out of circulation long enough for free O2 to accumulate. Lead with the inversion of the standard schoolbook story: photosynthesis alone isn't enough; the answer is that subduction has to hide the iron and sulfide chemistry that would otherwise eat the oxygen. Mechanism worth teaching: planetary habitability is a geophysics problem as much as a biology one, and the implications for exoplanet detection are direct — a stagnant-lid world like Venus can host life chemistry but cannot store its atmospheric exhaust. Reader takeaway: the question 'why does Earth have breathable air' has a new answer this week, and it's a tectonic answer.

stories.label: Discovery of furtivovirus advances understanding of giant virus evolution
stories.summary: A newly described giant virus — 'furtivovirus' — sits awkwardly on the edge of the classical tree of life, with a genome large enough to look cellular but no cellular machinery of its own. Lead with what the name acknowledges: it hides in plain sight, between virus and proto-cell, and challenges the cleanest line biology has drawn. Mechanism worth teaching: giant viruses keep getting weirder — they encode their own metabolic enzymes, in some cases translation factors — and each new isolate forces the question of whether 'life' has one origin or several. Reader takeaway: the next major revision of the tree of life is unlikely to be a tweak; it will be a redrawn topology, and furtivovirus is one of the branches forcing the change.

stories.label: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package
stories.summary: A critical vulnerability in Starlette/FastAPI's ASGI handling — used as the HTTP backbone for millions of AI agents and MCP servers — lets attackers walk in and steal credentials, tool tokens, and downstream third-party access. Lead with the dependency surface: the same week the [[agentic-divide-ai-agent-inequality-global-south-productivity]] story landed, the agent stack the global North relies on turns out to be one Python web framework deep. Mechanism worth teaching: agent supply chains are concentrated on a handful of HTTP servers, and a single misparsed header propagates to every downstream tool the agent can call — the blast radius is whatever the agent's OAuth scopes added up to. Reader takeaway: 'AI agents' are not yet a security category in their own right — they inherit the bugs of 2018-era Python web servers, and the credential exposure is qualitatively worse because the agents hold delegated keys.

stories.label: Charger placement optimization in wireless sensor networks using hybrid graph coloring and Enhanced Aquila Optimization
stories.summary: A two-stage optimization framework — hybrid graph coloring + an Enhanced Aquila metaheuristic — determines both the number and location of wireless chargers in sensor networks, the layer that decides how long an IoT deployment can actually survive on harvested energy. Lead with the deployment problem: as wireless sensor networks scale from a few hundred nodes to tens of thousands (smart-grid, water-quality, AMR monitoring), charger placement is the bottleneck most operators have been solving with rules of thumb. Mechanism worth teaching: graph coloring gives the lower bound on chargers needed; the bio-inspired Aquila search then tunes positions, an order of magnitude cheaper to compute than the integer-programming formulation. Reader takeaway: this is the unglamorous algorithmic infrastructure that decides whether the world's environmental-monitoring networks can run for a decade without rip-and-replace — and the answer is now substantially better.
